paragraphs.text: Sleep Duration and Memory Consolidation in Adolescents
Abstract
This short review summarises how sleep duration and sleep spindles relate to learning in teenagers. We argue that school start times should move later.
1. Introduction

Adolescents sleep less than they did a generation ago [1]. Short sleep is linked to poorer next-day recall of new material [2]. Sleep spindles strongly improve memory consolidation in every age group [3]. About 70% of high school students report insufficient sleep. Later school start times raised average attendance by 9% in a large district trial [4].
2. Discussion
Taken together, these results suggest that sleep is a modifiable driver of learning [1, 2]. We therefore recommend delaying the first bell.

Sleep Duration and Memory Consolidation in Adolescents
Abstract
This short review summarises how sleep duration and sleep spindles relate to learning in teenagers. We argue that school start times should move later.
1. Introduction

Adolescents sleep less than they did a generation ago [1]. Short sleep is linked to poorer next-day recall of new material [2]. Sleep spindles strongly improve memory consolidation in every age group [3]. About 70% of high school students report insufficient sleep. Later school start times raised average attendance by 9% in a large district trial [4].
2. Discussion
Taken together, these results suggest that sleep is a modifiable driver of learning [1, 2]. We therefore recommend delaying the first bell.
References
[1] Alvarez, M., Chen, L. (2019). Secular trends in adolescent sleep duration. Journal of Sleep Epidemiology.
[2] Okafor, T. (2020). Restricted sleep and word recall in teenagers. Learning and Sleep Research.
[3] Brandt, K., Silva, R. (2021). Sleep spindles and overnight retention across the lifespan. Memory Systems Journal.
[4] Novak, P. (2018). School start times and attendance: a district trial. Education Policy Quarterly.

/* ---------- filters + summary bar ---------- */
/* A claim sits in one group, by its best source. A claim that also has a cited source which
   does not support it is counted and filtered under "Not supported" as well, so that
   finding is never hidden behind a better result from another source. */
var active={};
var counts={ok:0,part:0,bad:0,unv:0,unc:0};
items.forEach(function(it){counts[it.group]++;});
function inGroup(it,g){return it.group===g||(g==='bad'&&it.failing)||(g==='prov'&&it.prov);}
function shown(it){return Object.keys(active).some(function(g){return active[g]&&inGroup(it,g);});}
var alsoFailing=items.filter(function(it){return it.failing;}).length;
var chips=$('#chips');
Object.keys(GLABEL).forEach(function(g){
  var b=el('button','chip g-'+g);b.type='button';b.setAttribute('aria-pressed','false');b.dataset.g=g;
  var n=counts[g]+(g==='bad'?alsoFailing:0);
  b.append(document.createTextNode(GLABEL[g]+' '));b.append(el('b',null,String(n)));
  b.title='Show only: '+GLABEL[g];
  if(g==='bad'&&alsoFailing)b.title='Includes '+alsoFailing+(alsoFailing===1?' claim that another source supports in part, but one':' claims that another source supports in part, but one')+' cited source does not support';
  b.addEventListener('click',function(){active[g]=!active[g];applyFilter();});
  chips.append(b);
});
var provCount=items.filter(function(it){return it.prov;}).length;
var judgedCount=items.filter(function(it){return it.group==='ok'||it.group==='part'||it.group==='bad';}).length;
if(provCount){

  pc.append(document.createTextNode('Abstract only '));pc.append(el('b',null,String(provCount)));

  pl.textContent=provCount+' of '+count(judgedCount,'result rests','results rest')+' on an abstract only (striped). '+(provCount===1?'It is':'They are')+' provisional: the full text is what settles '+(provCount===1?'it.':'them.');
}

function buildCard(i){

  if(it.kind==='claim'&&d.retracted)head.append(pill('Retracted source','var(--bad)',true));
  head.append(el('span','sp'));
  var onSources=!srcView.hidden;
  var pb=iconBtn('prev','Previous claim'),nb=iconBtn('next','Next claim'),cb=iconBtn('close','Close');
  pb.addEventListener('click',function(){go(-1);});nb.addEventListener('click',function(){go(1);});cb.addEventListener('click',closeCard);

    go2.addEventListener('click',function(ev){ev.preventDefault();showClaim(i);});
    where.append(go2);body.append(where);
  }
  card.append(body);
}

claims.claim_text: Sleep spindles strongly improve memory consolidation in every age group [3].
claims.paragraph_text: Adolescents sleep less than they did a generation ago [1]. Short sleep is linked to poorer next-day recall of new material [2]. Sleep spindles strongly improve memory consolidation in every age group [3]. About 70% of high school students report insufficient sleep. Later school start times raised average attendance by 9% in a large district trial [4].
